name: unknown-field-in-update-payload
description: An undeclared field in the PAYLOAD of an `update`, not in its address. `unknown-field-swc-safety-level` puts the undeclared name in the address, where an address step has to resolve against the registry to be taken at all; here every step resolves and the offending name rides inside the replacement value, one level down, where Pydantic's `extra="ignore"` would drop it and the change set would report success with an empty delta.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model. `ExampleSWC` carries one port `pOut`, and the registry declares `port` with exactly `name`, `direction`, `interface` and `description` — `safety_level` is a plausible name none of them is.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the requested address exactly, so the refusal is about the payload and not about authorization. That is the whole point of the vector: gate 1 and gate 2 both pass, and only the binding of the payload against the registry can find this.

input.intent: Record the ASIL level of the pOut port.

expected.notes: `unknown-field` is a field the REGISTRY does not declare, with no restriction to an address step, and the detection order lists it among pass B's codes. So an `update`'s replacement value is bound exactly as a `create`'s payload is, at every depth and under every verb: the same request written as a whole-collection `update` at `[ports]`, or as a `create` of the element with this port inside it, is refused with the same code at the same address. The address the violation names is the field's own — where the client wrote it — and not the address the operation carried. The model stays byte-identical.
